answer: In an island market trading onyx, each agent must lock $100 of collateral for 30 days before it can bid on jobs at dawn. A contract slashes the bond if the agent signs conflicting receipts for the same delivery, which anyone can prove by submitting both signatures. Creating names remains free, but activating 1,000 fake bidders immobilizes $100,000, and provable cheating burns their bonds; splitting into identities does not multiply capital.
